note: Score honestly. Most first-pass profiles land in the 30s to 50s. A stranger lands here from one reel and decides in a few seconds whether to follow, so the parts they read first carry the most points.

items.label: Name field
items.full_marks: The bold line under the photo (30 characters) holds the name plus the words someone would type into Instagram search to find this kind of account, for example 'Sam Lee | Home workouts for dads'. Instagram search reads this line.
items.common_fail: Only a first and last name, or a name with emoji, so the account never shows up when people search the topic.

items.label: Bio, first line
items.full_marks: The first line tells a stranger who this account is for and what they get from following, in words that audience would use themselves.
items.common_fail: A list of identities ('Founder | Gym rat | Dad'), a vague motto, or a job title nobody outside the industry understands.

items.label: Proof or offer
items.full_marks: The rest of the bio gives one reason to believe (a real number, a result, a name people know) or one clear thing to get, written as a sentence.
items.common_fail: Nothing that backs up the first line, or a wall of keywords and emoji.

items.label: Pinned posts
items.full_marks: Three posts are pinned and each does a different job: one shows proof, one explains what the account offers, one introduces the person. They were chosen on purpose.
items.common_fail: Nothing pinned, or three random old hits that don't tell a new visitor anything about the account today.

items.label: Link
items.full_marks: One link that matches what the bio promises: the free thing, the offer, or the next step. Two at the most.
items.common_fail: No link, a broken one, or a link page with so many buttons that nobody clicks any of them.

items.label: Highlights
items.full_marks: Four to six highlights that answer what a new follower wants to know (results, how it works, about me, the offer), with matching covers and names that make sense at a glance.
items.common_fail: No highlights, or a long row of old trips and events named with emoji only.

items.label: Grid covers
items.full_marks: The first nine covers are readable as tiny thumbnails and make the topic of the account obvious without opening anything. Covers are picked, often with a few words of text.
items.common_fail: Nine blurry frames of a face mid-sentence, so the grid says nothing about what the account is.

items.label: Profile photo
items.full_marks: A recent, well-lit face that fills most of the circle, with a plain background, recognisable at tiny size.
items.common_fail: A logo on a personal account, a far-away full-body shot, or a dark, old photo.

items.label: Handle
items.full_marks: Easy to say out loud and spell after hearing it once, and the same on the other platforms.
items.common_fail: Extra underscores, swapped letters or numbers that nobody can remember.

items.label: Account setup
items.full_marks: A creator or business account, with a category that fits the content and a contact option that someone actually checks.
items.common_fail: A personal account (no insights, no contact button), or a category that doesn't match the content.

items.label: Recent activity
items.full_marks: A post in the last seven days, and the comments on the latest posts are answered.
items.common_fail: Weeks since the last post, or a pile of comments nobody replied to, so the account looks abandoned.

items.label: Stories
items.full_marks: A story is up now, or the account posts stories most days, so a visitor sees a real person behind it.
